concepts.description: The 18th-century shift in Britain from agrarian and handicraft production to mechanized factory manufacturing. The document treats it as the central event whose preconditions and consequences it traces.
concepts.name: Industrial Revolution

concepts.description: The technology that transformed manufacturing during the Industrial Revolution by providing a new source of mechanical energy for factories.
concepts.name: Steam Power

concepts.description: The concentration of workers in factory towns as industrial production drew labor away from rural areas.
concepts.name: Urbanization

concepts.description: Legislation that followed public concern over working conditions in factories, representing the regulatory response to industrial labor problems.
concepts.name: Factory Acts

concepts.description: The labor environment in factories that became a public concern and ultimately prompted government regulation.
concepts.name: Working Conditions

concepts.description: The open system of patents that the document cites as one of the preconditions enabling British industrialization.
concepts.name: Patent Regime

concepts.description: The navigable waterways and routes that supported industrialization by moving goods and materials, listed as a key precondition.
concepts.name: Transport Network

concepts.description: Low-cost coal, identified as a foundational precondition that fueled the Industrial Revolution's energy needs.
concepts.name: Cheap Coal
